dedupe_keys.name: cost benefit prioritisation of rehabilitating nautical bottlenecks on an inland waterway corridor

description: This study by Bianca Duldner-Borca, Lisa-Maria Putz and Edwin van Hassel (European Transport Research Review, 2026) develops a modular cost-benefit analysis tool for ranking projects that rehabilitate nautical bottlenecks, such as shallow or narrow stretches, on inland waterways, and demonstrates it on a defined transport corridor. Coverage: for each bottleneck the tool calculates net present value and benefit-cost ratio, and for neighbouring bottleneck combinations it calculates marginal net present values; a greedy algorithm then ranks the investments. The results show strong path dependency: benefits arise only when all bottlenecks on the corridor have been rehabilitated, and isolated measures are mostly ineffective. Format and access: an open access journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: the authors call for real transport and vessel data and for ecological effects to be added, so the corridor results rest on modelled inputs. The corridor-level benefit logic can be used to rank waterway maintenance and dredging projects in network flow and investment optimisation models of inland shipping. It relates to the Albert Canal lock adaptation and the EuRIS notices to skippers data in the catalogue.
